conflict_topics: stove availability / weeknight cooking schedule (late-slot rota)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants offered concrete, practical proposals rather than only complaints (A proposing rule and rota; D requesting a guaranteed evening).
Immediate problem solved by a volunteer rather than prolonged negotiation: 'I'll wash it now.' (Turn 3).
Few repetitive exchanges; C restates the washing rule twice ('But everyone must stick to Agent A's rule...').
Commitments to finalise details were explicitly delegated to the group chat, keeping the face-to-face talk compact.
evaluation.final_reason: Housemates agreed to a standing cleaning rule and a concrete scheduling compromise. Key agreed items: Agent A's rule 'whoever uses a shared pan washes it the same night.' (Turn 1) Agent C volunteered to address the immediate problem: 'I'll wash it now.' (Turn 3). For the scheduling conflict Agent A proposed 'each of us gets one guaranteed late slot per week; the other weeknights are open' and instructed swaps via group chat (Turn 5); other agents accepted the rota in principle and committed to post their chosen nights in the chat (Turns 9,10,12,13). Thus the sanitation issue was volunteered and addressed and the stove-access issue was settled by a shared rota arrangement accepted by the group.
position_change_notes: Agent A proposed rules and a rota and maintained that solution throughout (Turn 1, Turn 5).
Agent B initially demanded immediate action and accepted the cleaning rule and rota quickly ('Okay, that rule works.' Turn 2; 'The rota's fine.' Turn 6).
Agent C moved from complaint to action: noticed the dirty pan, pledged to wash it ('I'll wash it now.' Turn 3), and reiterated the agreed rule (Turn 8).
Agent D introduced the scheduling demand (need for a guaranteed late slot) and then accepted the proposed rota and committed to post their slot (Turns 4, 13).

round_scores.evidence: Agent A proposes a household rule: 'whoever uses a shared pan washes it the same night.' Agent B accepts the rule but demands immediate action: 'Whoever used the pan last night, please wash it now; if no one does, Agent A, can you wash it so the smell stops? I need to sleep early.' A substantive incompatible state remains (dirty shared pan/smell; no one confirmed washing).

Agent C volunteers to wash the pan: 'I'll wash it now.' C and D both endorse the proposed washing rule. D raises a separate, substantive scheduling demand: 'I still can't really use the stove on weeknights — ... Can we do a short weeknight rota or give everyone one late slot...' The immediate cleaning is offered, but the scheduling conflict is explicit and unresolved.

Agent A proposes a concrete rota: 'each of us gets one guaranteed late slot per week; the other weeknights are open... If you can't make your slot, swap on the group chat.' Agent B accepts: 'The rota's fine.' The main disagreement (how to make stove access fair) has a concrete compromise proposal that others begin to accept; only minor administrative confirmation remains.

Agent A asks Agent C to carry out the immediate cleaning: 'Agent C, you said you'd wash it — can you do it now...' Agent C confirms: 'Okay — I'll wash it now. ... We'll finalise the weeknight rota in the chat.' Immediate sanitation is being addressed; the rota is deferred to the chat but accepted in principle.

Agent D requests concrete confirmations in chat; Agent A posts a slot: 'I'll confirm mine in the chat — Friday works for me.' Only minor outstanding action (others posting their chosen nights) remains; no substantive opposition is present.

Agent C and Agent D commit to add their late slots in the chat: 'Okay — I'll add my late slot in the chat tonight.' and 'Okay. I'll add my slot in the chat now.' The household has mutually accepted the cleaning norm ('whoever uses a shared pan washes it the same night') and a concrete rota scheme ('each of us gets one guaranteed late slot per week; ... swap on the group chat'). The immediate cleaning was volunteered and affirmed earlier ('I'll wash it now'), and scheduling was accepted and being confirmed by members.

substantive_insights: The conflict split into an immediate sanitation problem (dirty pan/smell) and an ongoing resource-allocation problem (fair stove access on weeknights).
Immediate sanitation was resolved quickly by a volunteer (C) after a clear rule was proposed; this removed the urgent impact (smell) while the longer-term scheduling was negotiated.
The scheduling tension was resolved via an explicit, shareable mechanism (one guaranteed late slot per person per week plus swaps), illustrating a compromise that balances recurring needs.
